narrative: Material PL1__M7609E01 exhibits moderate demand variability (CV=0.268) with no detectable trend across 84 working-day observations, following an approximately normal distribution. Lead times are severely unstable (CV=1.09, range 0.11–6.84 days), making lead-time variance the dominant driver of required safety stock. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity (7,674 units) was selected; the MOQ of 1,675 is non-binding. The recommended safety stock of 2,318 units represents a critical improvement over the current ERP setting of zero, required to achieve the 95% service level target under prevailing supply uncertainty.
warnings: Lead time CV = 1.09 is highly unstable — supplier performance management recommended
Safety stock increase from 0 to 2,318 units adds ~$777.85/yr in holding cost — justified for 95% SL

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous, fully non-zero, and moderately variable — well-suited to a fixed-reorder-point, fixed-order-quantity policy. EOQ (7,674) greatly exceeds MOQ (1,675), so the economic quantity governs. The policy is capacity-feasible with ~700-unit headroom.
research_insights.boundary_risk: No capacity constraint binds. Post-replenishment stock (9,992 units) remains below max_storage_units (10,692) by approximately 700 units — a thin but adequate buffer. If safety stock is revised upward, storage capacity should be re-checked.
